page: Google Cloud Platform c4a-highmem-1 is an Arm-based virtual machine instance belonging to the c4a server family. It features a single dedicated physical core powered by an Arm Neoverse-V2 processor architecture, operating with one thread per core. The instance is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8 GB per core. It does not include local NVMe storage or integrated GPU hardware, relying entirely on network-attached storage for boot and data volumes.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-threaded execution in specific workloads, such as gzip compression and bzip3 decompression, which both scored in the top 25% of tested systems. However, its overall compute and memory bandwidth capabilities are constrained by the single-core configuration. The instance recorded poor multi-core CPU performance and weak memory bandwidth, particularly during large-block uncached read and write operations. Database operations and Redis SET performance also fell into the lower percentiles, reflecting the throughput limitations of a single-vCPU environment.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c4a-highmem-1 offers a low-cost entry point into Arm64 development with a generous memory allocation relative to its compute capacity. It is best suited for lightweight, memory-sensitive workloads that do not require high parallel processing power. Appropriate use cases include small-scale web serving, single-threaded data processing tasks, lightweight caching layers, and software development or testing environments optimized for the Arm64 architecture.
